_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for Kinetic Scenes roadmap rendered at /kinetic-scenes/roadmap. Hand-maintained: update task `status` (planned, in-progress, done) as work lands in the UnysonPlus-Kinetic-Scenes repository, and `extensionVersion` to the Studio version.

milestones.title: Phase 1 · Foundations
milestones.goal: The parts everything else stands on: the project, the scene file, the player that plays it, the responsive stage and the route to the live site. At the end of this phase a hand-written scene file plays correctly on the subdomain.

tasks.title: Project scaffold
tasks.detail: A GitHub repository with a React + TypeScript editor built by Vite, and a separate plain-JavaScript player package. Both build to static files.

tasks.title: Scene file, version 1
tasks.detail: The JSON format with tracks, clips, preset settings, keyframes, assets and breakpoints, plus a schema that validates it and a version number so later formats can upgrade older files.

tasks.title: Player runtime
tasks.detail: Reads a scene file and builds one GSAP timeline. Seekable and repeatable: no unseeded randomness and no real-time physics, so any frame can be shown exactly.

tasks.title: Responsive stage
tasks.detail: An aspect ratio per breakpoint, the three height modes (**ratio**, **ratio capped to the window**, **fill the window**), sizes in CSS container units, and a safe-area guide.

tasks.title: Deploy to the subdomain
tasks.detail: A GitHub Action builds the editor and publishes it to GitHub Pages at `kinetic-scenes.unysonplus.com` (HTTPS) on every push to main.

milestones.title: Phase 2 · Editor
milestones.goal: The working studio: a canvas, a timeline and a first preset library, enough to build a hero animation by hand from start to finish.

tasks.title: Canvas and layers
tasks.detail: Text, image and shape layers on the stage; click to select, drag to move with snapping to the centre and the safe area, resize with handles, and double-click to edit text in place.

tasks.title: Multiple selection, Align and Distribute
tasks.detail: Select several layers with Shift or Ctrl + click, a dragged box or Ctrl+A; move them together; align their edges or centres to each other, the stage or the safe area; distribute them by edge, centre or equal gaps; and lock layers so they stay put.

tasks.title: Groups
tasks.detail: Group layers (Ctrl+G) to manage big scenes: a group has a timeline of its own, opens with a double-click (breadcrumb, everything else dimmed, Escape steps back), moves in time as one by dragging its bar, and takes presets as a whole. Ungrouping keeps every layer where and when it was.

tasks.title: Timeline
tasks.detail: Tracks and clips; drag, trim and move clips; a playhead with frame-accurate scrubbing; zoom; play, pause and loop.

tasks.title: Inspector
tasks.detail: Edit the selected clip's settings (text, image, colours, duration, easing), with per-breakpoint overrides for position, size and type size.

tasks.title: Preset library, first set
tasks.detail: 22 presets in a drag-and-drop panel, each with a live preview on hover: text (rise, slam, stretch, scramble, typewriter, blur, flip, tracking), reveal and exit (fade, wipe, iris, slide, grow), move and scale (pop, zoom, spin, keyframes) and emphasis (wave, pulse, shake, float, recolour).

tasks.title: Measured eases and better defaults
tasks.detail: Twelve named eases measured from professional motion pieces (Soft land, Snap and settle, Pop over, Leave…), each with what it is for. Exits default to an accelerating curve, staggered text gets a natural uneven rhythm, and the preset defaults follow measured timing.

tasks.title: Check scene
tasks.detail: A Check tab that reviews the scene as you work: text that leaves before it can be read, text too small on a screen size, text off the stage or on other text, clips fighting over a layer, long stretches with nothing moving. One-click fixes, Apply all, and Fix with AI.

tasks.title: Undo, redo and saving
tasks.detail: Full undo and redo (a drag is one step), the working scene saved in the browser automatically, and project files (`.scene.json`) to download and reopen.

tasks.title: Playback modes
tasks.detail: Play on load, play when scrolled into view, and loop or play once.

milestones.title: Phase 3 · Export
milestones.goal: Get a finished scene out of the Studio and onto a website.

tasks.title: Standalone HTML export
tasks.detail: One HTML file that contains the scene and the player and runs anywhere.

tasks.title: Embed snippet
tasks.detail: Copy-and-paste embed code from the Export window: the scene inline plus the player, loaded from its permanent versioned address. Works in any page that accepts HTML, such as a Custom HTML block in WordPress.

tasks.title: Images and fonts in exports
tasks.detail: Uploaded images travel inside the scene. Web fonts can be embedded in the downloaded page (Latin character sets packed in, others left linked), so it works offline.

tasks.title: Player versioning
tasks.detail: Downloaded pages carry their own copy of the player; embeds load a published player version that never changes. The build refuses to publish a changed player under an existing version number.

tasks.title: Accessibility
tasks.detail: Respect reduced-motion settings, keep text as real text, and give decorative layers the right hidden roles.

milestones.title: Phase 4 · Unyson+ integration
milestones.goal: Put Studio scenes into Unyson+ pages and share one preset library with the Animation Engine.

tasks.title: Page-builder element
tasks.detail: The **Kinetic Scene** element (Animation Engine → Kinetic Scene) plays a scene inside a Unyson+ page with the bundled player: paste the scene file or the embed code, and override the height mode, header height, start and loop for that placement.

tasks.title: Open in Studio
tasks.detail: **Open in Kinetic Scenes** opens the Studio with the element's scene; **Save to page** sends the edited scene straight back into the element. Each side only accepts messages from the other.

tasks.title: Shared preset library
tasks.detail: The Animation Engine's **Kinetic Scenes Preset** plays 39 of the Studio's presets (text, reveal, move and emphasis) on ordinary page elements, in view, on load, on hover or on click, with the Kinetic Scene element's own player (its new playPreset()), so an effect is built once. See [Presets on your pages](/kinetic-scenes/on-your-pages).

milestones.title: Phase 5 · AI
milestones.goal: Describe an animation in words and get an editable scene, using the AI Dev Kit on the user's own computer.

tasks.title: Studio-to-kit connection
tasks.detail: The Studio reaches the AI Dev Kit on the user's computer (`localhost:8787`). The kit only answers the Studio's own pages. Browsers ask once before a website may reach apps on the device; the Studio explains the prompt and what to do if it was refused.

tasks.title: Prompt to scene
tasks.detail: The AI tab turns a request into a scene file built only from the preset catalogue (sent with each request, so the kit never goes stale). The result is validated; an invalid answer gets one automatic repair round. It lands on the timeline as ordinary clips, one undo step.

tasks.title: Edit by prompt
tasks.detail: "Change this scene" or "Change the selected layers": the AI returns the whole scene with only the asked-for change, keeping every other layer and id, and re-checks the layout at every screen size so bigger text never overlaps or leaves the safe area.

tasks.title: AI assist panel
tasks.detail: A floating ✦ AI assist button over the stage opens a chat with the AI Dev Kit: who is answering, scope chips (this scene, the selected layers, a new scene), starter ideas, and for every answer one undo step, "Go back to before this" and a Check scene count. The Studio sends its motion rules with each request.

tasks.title: Custom code clip
tasks.detail: An escape hatch for effects no preset covers: a clip that runs your own GSAP code. It runs only where the page allows it (the Studio, your own exports, and WordPress pages by authors trusted with unfiltered HTML), a failing clip never stops the scene, and the AI never writes one.

tasks.title: AI Dev Kit hub
tasks.detail: The kit's dashboard opens on a Home page with a card per job (Site Converter, AI Assistant, Kinetic Scenes): whether each is ready, when it last called the kit and from which site, plus the AI in use. Retitled Unyson+ AI Dev Kit.

milestones.title: Phase 6 · 3D and finer control
milestones.goal: 3D objects on the timeline, and hand-keyframed motion for anything the presets don't cover.

tasks.title: 3D clips
tasks.detail: 3D layers drawn by three.js: extruded 3D text, shapes, extruded SVG logos and glTF/GLB models, with matte to chrome finishes and studio lighting. Spin 3D, Tumble in, Orbit and Camera push presets; every frame drawn from the timeline, so 3D seeks, loops and scroll-links. three.js loads only for scenes with a 3D layer.

tasks.title: Keyframe and curve editor
tasks.detail: Keyframes clips with a track per property (move, scale, rotation, opacity, blur), an ease per keyframe and custom curves drawn with two handles (overshoot and anticipation allowed). Add keyframes at the playhead, drag diamonds on the timeline, or drag the layer on the stage to set its position keyframe.

tasks.title: Scroll-linked playback
tasks.detail: Starts: As the page scrolls. The scroll position is the playhead, forwards and back. Pin while playing holds the stage below the header for a set number of screens; smoothing glides the playhead. Built without a scroll plugin, in the Studio, the exports and the Kinetic Scene element (with a Scroll length option), plus a Try scrolling test page.

tasks.title: More presets
tasks.detail: 35 presets in six groups, including Count up, Soft wipe, Blinds, Turn, Sheen, Drift, Gradient flow, Particles and the 3D set (Tumble in, Spin 3D, Orbit, Camera push), plus transitions between groups (Crossfade, Push, Zoom through, Soft wipe, Blinds, Iris, 3D turn) applied from the group Inspector.

tasks.title: Blender (add-on, coming soon)
tasks.detail: An installable add-on in the AI Dev Kit that has Blender build an elaborate 3D object from a description and save it as a glTF model for a 3D layer. Optional: the built-in 3D (text, shapes, SVGs and glTF) already draws live in the browser, and Blender is a large install.

milestones.title: Phase 7 · Later
milestones.goal: Useful additions once the core works, none of which change the scene file.

tasks.title: Video export
tasks.detail: Export → Video renders MP4 (H.264) or WebM (VP9) at Full HD, HD, 4K, vertical or square, 24 to 60 fps. The AI Dev Kit (1.12.34) draws the scene frame by frame in headless Chrome and encodes it with ffmpeg, so every frame is exact, 3D included.

tasks.title: Share links
tasks.detail: Export → Share link puts the whole scene, compressed, inside the link: anyone who opens it gets their own copy in the Studio. No account, no server and no storage; custom code clips are removed from shared scenes.

tasks.title: Save to Google Drive
tasks.detail: Projects on any computer without our own server: people sign in with Google and their scenes are saved to their own Drive. Planned if people ask for cross-device projects. Needs a Google OAuth client ID from the site owner before it can be built.

tasks.title: Accounts and cloud projects (only if needed)
tasks.detail: If real accounts are ever needed (a project library, short links, embeds that update in place), they run on a free cloud tier, separate from the website hosting, with uploads on object storage and embeds still served from GitHub Pages.

tasks.title: Click-to-advance presentations
tasks.detail: Timeline markers and Playback → Advance: On click. The scene stops at each marker until a click, a tap or the arrow keys, with a pulsing hint; full screen is a presenter mode; without motion it jumps slide to slide.

milestones.title: Phase 8 · Sound and voice
milestones.goal: Voice-overs, music and sound effects, and scenes made from a voice-over with AI.

tasks.title: Audio track
tasks.detail: Voice-overs, music and sound effects on the timeline with waveforms, trimming, volume and fades, played in step with the animation. Scenes with sound start muted on pages (a Tap for sound button), and video exports mix the sound in.

tasks.title: Built-in sound effects
tasks.detail: 25 sounds made by the player itself (whoosh, swish, pop, click, typing, impact, thud, riser, chime, sparkle, shimmer and more): nothing to download, identical in the Studio, on pages and in video exports. Give any clip a sound and it moves with the clip; Add suggested sounds places matching ones on a scene's key moments.

tasks.title: Sound library in the AI Dev Kit
tasks.detail: Search Freesound's public-domain (CC0) sounds from the Sounds tab with your own free key, through the AI Dev Kit (sounds are cached on your computer and added to the scene as audio). The planned one-click bulk download was dropped: the public CC0 packs could not be fetched reliably, and search covers far more sounds.

tasks.title: Generate a sound
tasks.detail: Describe a sound ("a soft paper swoosh, 0.6 s") and click Make: with an ElevenLabs key the AI Dev Kit generates it; otherwise the AI writes a synth recipe (oscillators, noise, filter and envelopes) that the Studio renders into a WAV in the browser, with no model to download.

tasks.title: Styles (scene presets)
tasks.detail: Eight ready looks (Night, Clean, Kinetic, Pastel, Neon, Editorial, Playful, Luxe), each a palette, a font pairing, a motion personality, a pace and a sound palette. Apply one to a scene (colours and fonts, motion and sounds, each optional), start a new scene in it, or give it to AI assist as art direction. Save your own scene as a style.

tasks.title: Brand kit
tasks.detail: Create a brand kit in the Styles tab: name, logo, five colours, fonts and weights, capitals and which built-in style it moves like. Brand styles add the logo to new scenes and AI assist uses it; any style exports and imports as a .json file to share with a team.

tasks.title: Transcription in the AI Dev Kit
tasks.detail: Select a voice-over and click Transcribe: whisper.cpp runs on your own computer through the AI Dev Kit (downloaded once, then offline; Fast 148 MB or Accurate 488 MB). Every word gets its time and an emphasis score from how loudly, how high and how long it is said, and the delivery is summarised (pace, energy). Words show on the timeline and a click jumps to one.

tasks.title: Make a scene from a voice-over
tasks.detail: Transcribe a voice-over, then click Make a scene from this voice-over: the words are grouped into beats (phrases between pauses and sentence ends) and AI assist builds kinetic type timed to them, the key words of each beat entering as they are said, the strongest words landing as hits with a sound, transitions at pauses, and motion matched to the delivery, in the style picked in AI assist. Check scene treats text the voice is saying as read by ear.

tasks.title: Studio tools for AI apps (MCP)
tasks.detail: The AI Dev Kit's studio-mcp.mjs gives AI apps such as Claude Desktop nine tools: check, inspect, stills and render a scene, beats and transcription, plus the scene guide (the format and presets), a Studio link that opens a scene in the browser, and saving a scene to a file. Scenes can be passed inline, so a conversation can make one from nothing.

tasks.title: Voice and music separation
tasks.detail: Separate voice and music, on footage and on audio clips, splits a clip's sound into a voice track and a music track in step with it: transcribe the voice alone for cleaner word times, remove or replace the music, or keep both (music is lowered under the voice). HTDemucs v4 runs in the AI Dev Kit through ONNX Runtime, on this computer; about 170 MB, downloaded once. Also the kit's separate command and audio_separate tool.

tasks.title: Sound identification (add-on, coming soon)
tasks.detail: An installable add-on in the AI Dev Kit that names the sounds in a clip (a door slam, a music hit, ambience) with an audio-labelling model, so AI assist can find and reuse moments in someone's own footage. Optional, because built-in sounds and Freesound results are already named.

tasks.title: Add-ons
tasks.detail: An Add-ons panel lists the extra tools the AI Dev Kit can use on this computer: connectors to apps the person installs (found automatically, or at a location set once) and downloads the kit installs itself. Voicebox is the first connector: its voice profiles speak voice-overs from a script, every word timed. See [Add-ons](/kinetic-scenes/addons). ACE-Step is the second connector: Make music adds an instrumental made on this computer as a Music track, beats found. A connector can be given its folder or program, so the kit starts the app when needed (and stops ACE-Step after ten idle minutes); when the kit is not found, the Studio links to it and its setup guide.

tasks.title: Kokoro voices (add-on)
tasks.detail: A second set of built-in voices from Kokoro, a small free text-to-speech model (Apache licence) that sounds more natural than the current voices and runs without a graphics card.

tasks.title: Check this computer
tasks.detail: One AI Dev Kit command, and a button in Add-ons, that lists what this computer has for Kinetic Scenes (the kit's version, ffmpeg, the rendering browser, each add-on and where it is, the graphics card and its free memory), ready to paste into a bug report.

milestones.title: Phase 9 · Fluid motion
milestones.goal: Scenes that flow like hand-made motion graphics: one element turning into the next, with transitions, a camera, drawn paths, glow and impact.

tasks.title: Scene transitions
tasks.detail: Six transitions made for whole groups: Slash (a glowing line sweeps across and reveals the next scene), Flash, Whip pan, Glitch, Dip to colour and Zoom through, each with its sound, alongside Crossfade, Push, Soft wipe, Blinds, Iris and 3D turn. Transition to the next group places the matched pair; the leaving group's own exits give way to it.

tasks.title: Whip and light-streak transitions
tasks.detail: The cut hand-made reels use most: a velocity-matched whip (the old scene accelerates out with heavy directional blur, the new one arrives from the same direction at the same speed and settles), and a light streak fired exactly at the cut to hide the join.

tasks.title: Camera
tasks.detail: One camera over every layer that pans, zooms, rolls and tilts in perspective, keyframed on its own Camera row with a curve per move, ready-made moves (push in, pull out, pans, tilt reveal, slow drift, Dutch roll) and a Camera view switch for editing the flat layout. Transitions stay exact under a moving camera.

tasks.title: Exact frames when jumping
tasks.detail: Jumping to a moment (scrubbing, seeking, video export) shows exactly what playing to it shows. The player's self-test now checks every frame where any of the 41 presets or a camera key starts or ends, plus the frames either side (231 frames, all identical), and video export takes each frame at an exact frame time, so a cut never lands a frame early or late.

tasks.title: Safer video export
tasks.detail: Before the first frame, video export waits for fonts, every image (loaded and decoded), images used as backgrounds and every 3D model, and tells you in the Studio if anything failed to load or ran out of time, instead of silently rendering blank frames.

tasks.title: Paths and drawn lines
tasks.detail: Lines, curves and connectors that draw themselves, layers that travel along a path (a comet that writes a word), and fading trails behind moving things.

tasks.title: Diagram layer
tasks.detail: Nodes and connections as one layer: flowcharts, architecture diagrams and branch graphs (lines that branch off and merge back, labels, and a tag that moves from node to node). Adding a node animates it in and its connections draw themselves; moving a node bends its connections with it. Stored as data, so the AI can write one and you can edit it.

tasks.title: Flow lines
tasks.detail: A bundle of glowing curves between two layers, made in one go: pick the start and end layers, how many lines, how far they fan out and squeeze together, their gradient colours and how strongly they glow (a soft halo under a bright core, brightening where lines cross). The lines draw themselves, light pulses or icons can flow along them, and they stay attached when either layer moves, so they work with the camera and with pinned layers. For showing data, work or ideas passing from one thing to another.

tasks.title: Repeat from a list
tasks.detail: Design one item (a row with a badge, a title and a subtitle, an app card, a step card), give it a list of entries, and get one copy per entry, laid out and staggered. Change the list and every copy updates; steps can point at an item by its position.

tasks.title: Change text
tasks.detail: A label or pill changes its text on cue ("booting" to "ready in 45 s", "1 / 10" to "2 / 10") with a quick slide, roll or fade, and its box resizes smoothly to fit the new words.

tasks.title: Word-reveal carrier
tasks.detail: A text preset where the first word slides in big and fast and each following word travels less (for example 360, 120, 60, 25, 12 px), so a line arrives with momentum instead of in a uniform stagger.

tasks.title: Image layers (AI)
tasks.detail: Split into layers: an image becomes a group of stacked transparent layers (background, subject, objects, text) in exactly the same place, so a picture can be revealed piece by piece instead of all at once, each part animated on its own. With a depth per layer, a camera move turns a flat photo into a 2.5D parallax shot. Runs through the AI Dev Kit: Qwen-Image-Layered through the user's own fal.ai key (or on a local GPU that can hold it), with a lighter local fallback (cutting out the subject and filling in behind it) that runs on an ordinary computer.

tasks.title: Glow and motion blur
tasks.detail: Neon glow on text and shapes, and blur along the direction of fast moves, so quick motion reads as speed rather than a jump.

tasks.title: Impact bursts
tasks.detail: One-off bursts of sparks, shards or rings on a hit, landing with the sound and the word they punctuate.

tasks.title: Captions with the spoken word highlighted
tasks.detail: Captions built from a transcribed voice-over that light up each word as it is said, in the style's colours, alongside or instead of the big kinetic type.

tasks.title: Picture leads the voice on punchlines
tasks.detail: In scenes made from a voice-over, a reveal finishes on its word instead of starting on it, so the picture lands as the word is heard (the viewer sees, then hears). Punchlines lead slightly; transcripts reach the AI as compact phrase lines, leaving more of its budget for the scene.

tasks.title: Music beat sync
tasks.detail: Drop music on the timeline and the Studio finds its tempo, beat grid and strongest moments, right in the browser (no Python): each beat scored by its onset strength, local contrast, loudness and bass. The beats show on the audio row; a big reveal can snap up to 0.15 s onto a strong moment and small entrances up to 0.10 s onto a beat, only a few are locked per scene, and text that must be read lands on every other beat at fast tempos. AI assist gets the same cue list.

tasks.title: Music-reactive glow
tasks.detail: A loudness and bass curve computed once from the music lets a few things breathe with it (a glow, a background's warmth, a card's presence). Precomputed, so it seeks and exports exactly; never equaliser bars or strobing.

tasks.title: Sound that sounds designed
tasks.detail: Fewer effects, each tied to something visible; each sound started early by its own attack so its hit lands on the frame; a softness rating on every built-in sound so repeated ones stay gentle; and video export mixed to a standard loudness (-14 LUFS, peaks under -1 dB) with music lowered under a voice-over.

tasks.title: Interface building blocks
tasks.detail: Ready-made pieces for product videos: a prompt box that types, highlighted tags, progress bars that fill over a set time, timer readouts ("21 s", "0:45"), stacking list cards, and dashed outlines that can march while something is working and turn solid when it is ready.

tasks.title: Code explainer kit
tasks.detail: Everything a coding explainer needs. A Code layer that shows real code with syntax colours, line numbers, a file tab and an optional window frame and Run button, stored as text so the AI can write it and you can edit it. A Type code preset that types it character by character with a blinking caret, in a natural rhythm (quick within a word, a short pause at punctuation and new lines) and line by line so it can follow a voice-over. Line and token highlights that aim at a line or a word in the code and follow it as it types or scrolls. A Terminal style for a prompt, a typed command and output appearing on cue. Callout pills with a connector that stay attached to the line they explain, and labelled value boxes for showing what a variable holds. With Explainer mode, AI assist can take a code file and a topic and build the whole video.

tasks.title: Code edits
tasks.detail: The Code layer changes existing code, not only writes new code: typing in the middle with the lines below sliding down smoothly, selecting and deleting, and turning one version into another (repeated lines becoming a function call). Autocomplete popups and parameter hints appear while typing, the editor scrolls to follow the caret, and a Run step shows the output panel. You describe the code as versions (before, after each step) and the Studio works out the keystrokes between them, timed to the voice-over through Steps.

tasks.title: Select box emphasis
tasks.detail: An emphasis preset that draws a coloured box with small square corner handles around one word of a headline, like a selected object in a design tool, with the word taking the box's colour. Useful well beyond code: heroes, product tours and social clips.

tasks.title: Morph between acts
tasks.detail: The same word, card or screenshot glides from its place in one act to its place in the next (position, size, colour and corner radius), instead of fading out and in again, so the viewer's eye never loses it.

tasks.title: Benchmark against hand-made videos
tasks.detail: Rebuild reference motion-graphics videos from their voice-overs with the new tools and compare them frame by frame, the way the Site Converter is measured against its sources, until the Studio's version holds up next to them. Round 1 rebuilt a 10-second side-by-side race explainer from the new pieces and fixed what it found (pills sized to their words, Change text resizing them smoothly); round 2 compares it frame by frame with the reference. Round 2 waits for the reference video.

milestones.title: Phase 10 · Product tours and interactive scenes
milestones.goal: Show Unyson+ (or any product) working, from screenshots instead of screen recordings: a cursor that moves, hovers and clicks, zooms into the part that matters, and scenes visitors can click, follow and explore. Links and the looping ending came first (a hero's call to action needs them now); hover effects next, then paths and drawn lines (Phase 9), then the tour tools.

tasks.title: Links on layers
tasks.detail: Any text, shape, image or group can be a link (a web address, a page on the same site, an anchor, email or phone; optionally a new tab). On the stage it is a click area; the real link sits in the scene's text for search engines and screen readers, so keyboard users reach it with Tab and the layer shows a focus ring. Other kinds of address are left out.

tasks.title: What happens at the end
tasks.detail: Stop on the last frame, loop everything, or loop the last part: after one full play, the scene repeats only from a moment you choose, so a closing call to action keeps breathing (and stays clickable) while the rest holds. Idle presets made for it (an endless glow, a slow breathe) are still to come.

tasks.title: Scroll a screenshot
tasks.detail: The Scroll preset scrolls a tall screenshot inside its frame (or pans a wide one across), from one point to another, so a real settings page or site can be shown moving inside a browser window, tilting with the camera.

tasks.title: Pin to the stage
tasks.detail: A layer or group can be pinned to the stage instead of the scene's frame: its position becomes a percentage of the stage, so badges, logos and corner calls to action sit in the real corner of any box the scene fills, whatever its shape. Sizes keep the frame's units; pinned layers stay put when the camera moves.

tasks.title: Layouts by shape
tasks.detail: Besides the layouts by width (desktop, tablet, phone), an extra layout for stages much wider than the design (an ultrawide hero), so the content can spread out instead of showing the page at the sides.

tasks.title: Hover effects
tasks.detail: Presets for layers people can point at (lift, grow, glow, brighten, a shine sweeping across, an underline drawing in, a colour change), and custom CSS for anything else where the page's author is trusted. Hovers never fight the animation, and on phones a tap just follows the link.

tasks.title: Cursors
tasks.detail: Built-in cursors drawn big enough to read in a video (about 7% of the frame wide in a full-frame scene), which enter from off-screen and leave the same way, never fade in on the spot, and change from an arrow to a pointing hand over buttons. The cursor carries the viewer's eye from one thing to the next, and its click visibly causes what happens next.

tasks.title: Move to a target
tasks.detail: Pick a layer (the Save button) and the cursor travels to it along a natural curve with real pointer easing, so a tour is built by pointing, not by keyframing.

tasks.title: Click effect
tasks.detail: The cursor presses, a ring ripples out, the button dips and a click sounds, all landing on the same frame.

tasks.title: Focus and spotlight
tasks.detail: Frame a region and the camera zooms to it; a spotlight dims everything else; a callout label points at the thing being explained.

tasks.title: Cut a piece out of a screenshot
tasks.detail: Drag a box over part of a screenshot (a button, a panel, a row) and it becomes its own layer in exactly the same place, ready to press, slide or glow, with the gap behind it filled from its surroundings. Interface screenshots are mostly rectangles, so this needs no AI.

tasks.title: Before and after states, and steps
tasks.detail: Swap to a second screenshot of the same screen exactly on the click frame (the menu opened, the setting saved), or type into a field, so actions have visible results. Beyond two states: a scene can be a sequence of steps, and each step says what changes (this row is active, the terminal shows this command, this box fills, this node appears, this counter reads 3 / 10). The Studio builds the timing, every panel stays in sync, and steps can be reordered or retimed as a whole. The AI describes a walkthrough as steps instead of placing hundreds of keyframes.

tasks.title: Hotspots
tasks.detail: Clickable areas that jump to a part of the scene, so a visitor can choose what to see next: an interactive demo instead of a single linear play.

milestones.title: Phase 11 · The AI director
milestones.goal: Make the AI Dev Kit the best motion designer of the tools out there, using only the AI subscription you already pay for (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor): no API keys, no per-use cost. The difference is not a bigger prompt but a way of working: the AI plans with you, builds, checks its work, looks at rendered frames, fixes what it sees and hands you a scene you can still edit, for a website or a video.

tasks.title: The Kinetic Scenes skill
tasks.detail: Everything an AI needs to make a good scene, written for any agent: the workflow, the scene format, every preset and its settings, the motion rules, styles and tones, sound, and a checklist. Generated from the Studio's own code on every release, so it never goes out of date; published at kinetic-scenes.unysonplus.com/skill/ (any AI can read it from a link) and copied into the AI Dev Kit for agents working on your computer.

tasks.title: Tools the AI can use
tasks.detail: The kit gives the AI hands and eyes: inspect (capture a website, read a project, transcribe a voice-over), check (the real validator and Check scene), stills (render frames to look at), beats (analyse music) and render (video export). Offered as kit commands and as a local MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can call them while they work.

tasks.title: Plan first
tasks.detail: For a new scene, the AI first writes a storyboard you can adjust: the hook in the first two seconds, the highlights, the ending, each act's length, what appears one by one, the transitions and the sound. It builds only once you agree, so long scenes come out right and you steer before the work is done.

tasks.title: Explainer mode
tasks.detail: A named mode in AI assist for explainer videos and heroes. Script first: the AI writes the narration and splits it into segments, each naming what the screen shows, and you approve or edit it before anything is built. The structure is a hook in the first two seconds, the problem, the product in use (entry, key action, result), why it matters and a call to action. The narration explains what the viewer sees instead of reading the screen aloud; every segment moves the picture (a cursor click, a focus, a state change, kinetic type for the key phrase), and each visual lands just before its words. Captions come from the narration, one line at a time. Then the AI director loop checks it, looks at rendered frames and fixes it. For coding tutorials the AI writes the script and the code for each step together, running the code first so the output on screen is real. You record the narration in your own voice (or make it with a local voice tool or the kit's built-in voice), the kit transcribes it with a time for every word, and the AI builds the timeline so every code change and caption lands on the word it belongs to. Any language the transcription supports works, including Filipino and Taglish.

tasks.title: Look, criticise, fix
tasks.detail: After building, the kit renders the settled frame of every act and the middle of every transition; the AI looks at them with the Check scene report, criticises its own work like a reviewer (cramped layouts, low contrast, muddy transitions, unreadable text) and fixes it, at most a few rounds. Only then does it show you the result.

tasks.title: Quick scene from a website or a project
tasks.detail: Paste a URL (or point at a project folder) and get a scene: the kit's capture service renders the site and takes its real colours, fonts, copy and screenshots; the AI plans and builds from them, shows the product in use rather than describing it, and never invents claims. The result is an editable scene that works as a hero and exports as a video.

tasks.title: Any of your subscriptions
tasks.detail: Your Claude subscription through the claude command (already working), your ChatGPT subscription through OpenAI's codex command, and Cursor through cursor-agent. The kit picks what you have; nothing needs an API key.

tasks.title: Voice-over from a script
tasks.detail: No microphone needed: the AI Dev Kit turns a script into a voice-over on your computer with a free local voice model (such as Kokoro), with no account or API. Every word arrives with its time, so the scene is built on the real narration (the audio is the clock), and changing a line regenerates only that part. Your own recording still works as before.

tasks.title: An AI inside the open Studio
tasks.detail: The Studio registers its own tools with the browser (WebMCP): look at the scene, inspect a layer, render a frame at any moment, edit text, move layers, add and change clips. An AI in the browser (ChatGPT Desktop already supports it; Chrome is trialling it) can then work on the scene in front of you, with every change in the normal undo history.

tasks.title: Better rules for every step
tasks.detail: The craft the best tools use, built into the rules and checks: tone presets that set structure (number of acts, hold lengths, transition style, sound density); one new thing at a time; no two acts in a row with the same entrance and layout; a pause of 0.3 to 0.75 s before a big payoff; entrances under about 0.8 s; two or three transition styles per scene; no muddy crossfade between two busy layouts.

tasks.title: The best still frame, picked for you
tasks.detail: The Still frame (what visitors who turn off animation see, and a video's thumbnail) is suggested automatically: the most complete settled moment, with every word in and nothing mid-transition.

tasks.title: Check the layout
tasks.detail: Every part of a scene is reviewed at the moment it has fully landed. The player measures the drawn frame there (words on words, words crossing or crowding a panel, ticks far from their words, uneven or off-centre lists, words off the stage); the Studio's Check tab runs it on request, the kit's stills and check report it, and AI assist fixes every item before looking at the frames against a written review list. Ticks and strikes now sit beside the words, not at the edge of the text box.

milestones.title: Phase 12 · Video mode
milestones.goal: A motion-graphics companion for video creators who edit elsewhere: make kinetic type, backgrounds, objects and effects to layer over Reels, TikToks, Shorts and YouTube videos. Web stays the main mode.

tasks.title: Web and Video modes
tasks.detail: Choose what a scene is for when you start it, and switch later. Web (the default) keeps responsive layouts, scroll and click playback, search-engine text and the WordPress element. Video sets one fixed format, plays once at an exact length, puts sound first and shows the tools and checks that suit video.

tasks.title: Video formats and platform safe zones
tasks.detail: 9:16 (1080×1920), 1:1, 4:5 and 16:9 at a chosen frame rate, with guides for where TikTok, Reels and Shorts cover the picture with their buttons and captions.

tasks.title: Transparent overlay export
tasks.detail: Export the motion graphics alone, with a transparent background (WebM with alpha, or ProRes 4444), ready to drop on top of footage in CapCut, Premiere or DaVinci Resolve. MP4 for finished pieces, and a cover image.

tasks.title: Your footage as a reference or background
tasks.detail: Bring in a video or photo to design against: line up type and effects with what happens on camera, then export the graphics alone or the full composite.

tasks.title: Video checks and AI rules
tasks.detail: Check scene and AI assist tuned for video: a hook in the first seconds, scene pacing, caption ratios, platform length limits and loudness.

tasks.title: One project, several formats
tasks.detail: Lay a scene out once for 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9 and export them together.

tasks.title: Video export without the AI Dev Kit
tasks.detail: Investigated. WebCodecs can encode video in the browser, but a page has no exact way to turn its own HTML into frames: the options today are recording the screen in real time (not frame-exact, and it asks permission) or the experimental HTML-in-Canvas proposal (drawing elements into a canvas), which is not in browsers yet. Video export stays with the AI Dev Kit, which renders every frame exactly; revisit when HTML-in-Canvas ships.

tasks.title: Simple video tools (later)
tasks.detail: Light trimming and speed changes for footage layers. Editing stays the job of a video editor; the Studio is for what goes on top.

tasks.title: Videos that feel like one camera move
tasks.detail: For videos (not website loops): how a scene leaves sets how the next one arrives (same direction and speed, cutting mid-motion), one main direction for the whole film with other directions saved for meaning, causes and effects on the same frame, and no idle floating to fill time: every second something tells the story. A check measures every cut.

milestones.title: Phase 13 — Video editing effects
milestones.goal: The effects short-form editors use on talking-head videos, about 45 of them, as presets you can drop on a clip and as named effects AI assist can place for you ("add a gravity drop on the word drop"). Built on the footage layer from Phase 12. About a third can already be built by hand from today's presets; this phase makes each one a single preset or ready-made piece, adds what is missing, and adds the two things a third of them need: cutting the person out of the footage, and following them.

tasks.title: Cut the person out of the footage
tasks.detail: The AI Dev Kit separates the person from the background in every frame (on your computer, no upload) and adds them as a see-through footage layer above the graphics. That unlocks: words behind the person (magazine cover, a headline behind the head), paper cut-out (a white outline on a coloured backdrop), a new background (green screen, studio reveal), the background shattering while the person stays (frame break), stepping out of a frame (frame escape) and dolly zoom (background and person zooming opposite ways).

tasks.title: Follow the person
tasks.detail: The kit finds the face (or a chosen point) in every frame and turns it into a path a layer can follow: a hand-drawn circle that stays on the face (live markup), icons orbiting the head (orbit), captions or a callout that move with the speaker, a zoom that keeps the face centred.

tasks.title: Effects on footage
tasks.detail: Presets for a footage layer: snap zoom (a sharp punch-in), digital zoom (zoom, blur and a recording frame), colour grades that animate (black and white, warm, cool, film), the grade wiping across with a before / after handle (grade slider, eyedropper grade, mood curtain), projected film (sprocket edges, flicker, grain), film look, a liquid-glass lens that bends the picture as it passes, and a picture-in-picture portal the video flies into.

tasks.title: Frames and copies of the footage
tasks.detail: Show footage (or an image) inside a phone, a browser, a polaroid, a film strip or a video card, and in copies: a playing grid, a contact sheet filling up, a picture dive (the frame inside the frame inside the frame), a title card that dives into the phone.

tasks.title: Text effects from short-form video
tasks.detail: Gravity drop (letters fall, bounce and settle), headline storm (tilted headline strips flying in and stacking), knockout captions (words cut out of a block, the video showing through), giant captions and viral drop caption styles, receipt printer (a slip printing out of a slot), screenplay page (typed, then highlighted), intertitle (a silent-film card), title card with a running timecode, and an odometer counter with rolling digits.

tasks.title: Emphasis presets
tasks.detail: Strike (a line drawn through, then the thing falls away), jiggle (the phone-home-screen wobble before a delete), checklist pop (items ticking on one by one beside the speaker), and a flat orbit (things circling a point).

tasks.title: Ready-made UI pieces
tasks.detail: Animated pieces to drop in and edit: a comment box that types and gets a reply (comment CTA, comment drop), a prompt bar, a chat window, a file drop zone, an editing timeline, a social feed scrolling past, a fan of storyboard cards, a growth chart that climbs with its counter, a row of app icons, and an effects checklist that counts up.

tasks.title: AI assist that edits your video
tasks.detail: Every effect is a named recipe AI assist knows. Drop in raw footage and say what you want: the kit transcribes it, adds captions, and places effects on the moments that suit them (a gravity drop on the word it names, a snap zoom on the punchline, a comment CTA at the end), all as ordinary clips you can change.

tasks.title: Loadout piece
tasks.detail: Five locked slots fill one by one while a counter steps 0/5 to 5/5 and a card names each item: a stack, a toolkit, the steps of a setup.

milestones.title: Phase 14 — Faster, and video without the kit
milestones.goal: Make the slow parts quick and remove the last thing that needs the AI Dev Kit: editing a video with AI in under a minute, cutting the person out on the graphics card, and exporting video from the browser itself where the browser can draw a page into a picture.

tasks.title: A faster Edit my video
tasks.detail: The AI answers with only what it adds (new layers and clips), and Look and fix with only the layers it changes, instead of rewriting the whole scene; the Studio and the AI Dev Kit merge them in. The AI's own call went from about 5 minutes to under 2 with Claude Code's default model; a faster model chosen in the AI Dev Kit brings it under a minute.

tasks.title: Cut-out on the graphics card
tasks.detail: The person is cut out on the graphics card (WebGPU) where the computer has one: about 50 ms a frame on a graphics card instead of about 650 ms on the processor, which stays the fallback.

tasks.title: Video export in the browser
tasks.detail: Where the browser can draw part of a page into a picture (HTML-in-Canvas; in Chrome behind an experimental setting today), the Studio renders the video itself with nothing installed: each frame exact, encoded by the browser (H.264 and AAC) into an MP4. Elsewhere, and for see-through or ProRes video, the AI Dev Kit renders it.

milestones.title: Phase 15 — Approachable, and proven
milestones.goal: The editor can already do a great deal; this phase makes it easy for someone who has never used a timeline to make and export a good animation in a few minutes, and backs its claims with tests. Prompted by outside reviews: the concept rated highly, ease of adoption and production readiness were the weak spots.

tasks.title: Your first scene in two minutes
tasks.detail: A guided first run for new visitors, built on the Studio's own tour tools (cursor, spotlight, callouts): pick a starting point, change the words, watch it play, export. Skippable, offered once, reopenable from Help. The aim: a polished result before reading any of the manual.

tasks.title: Start from a template
tasks.detail: Complete, ready-to-use scenes by goal, not by technique: website hero, product reveal, feature list, pricing, call to action, logo intro, social promo, explainer and code walkthrough. Shown when starting a new scene (File, New) and in the library, each in the person's brand kit when they have one. Every template passes Check scene and the settled-frame layout review before it ships.

tasks.title: Presets by what you want to do
tasks.detail: A second way to browse the presets, by goal ("make a headline land", "reveal a picture", "draw attention", "change scenes") alongside today's technique groups, with plain-language names next to motion terms, so people who do not know motion vocabulary still find the right one.

tasks.title: What works without AI, and what AI adds
tasks.detail: One clear screen, and a section on the overview: the editor, export and video work free with no AI at all; the AI Dev Kit adds local tools (speech, voices, separation, rendering); AI assist needs an AI connected through it (your own subscription or a local model). Shown the first time someone opens AI assist or Add-ons.

tasks.title: Lead with the result, standalone first
tasks.detail: Rewrite the overview and the Studio's first screen around the result ("Create professional motion graphics for websites and video, without starting from scratch or writing animation code"), not the number of presets. Present Kinetic Scenes as a standalone tool that works on any website, with Unyson+ and WordPress as an added advantage rather than a requirement.

tasks.title: Tested and published: browsers, phones, big scenes, video, WordPress
tasks.detail: A repeatable test run, published on the docs: current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari (desktop and iOS); playback smoothness on a mid-range phone; scenes with 100+ layers and long timelines; video export in every format, in the AI Dev Kit and in the browser; the Kinetic Scene element in WordPress with common themes, page builders and caching plugins. Failures become fixes or documented limits.

tasks.title: Known limitations and support
tasks.detail: A plain page: which browsers are supported, where projects are saved (this browser, project files) and what that means, what each export carries (fonts, footage, sound), the version promise for embeds, and what is not supported yet.

tasks.title: One source of truth for the version and stage
tasks.detail: The Studio publishes its own version and release stage (Beta) in a small file at build time; the docs, the roadmap and the overview read it instead of a number typed by hand, so the editor and the documentation can never disagree.

tasks.title: Decide: free or paid, and where projects are saved
tasks.detail: Settle the two open questions on the overview (whether the Studio stays free with AI optional, and whether projects get cloud saving and accounts), and record the reasons in the Design Decisions log.

tasks.title: Explainer template
tasks.detail: A ready-made explainer layout for longer scenes (2-8 minutes): chapter cards, a chapter progress bar, a small heads-up label and subtitles, built from a script by AI assist one part at a time, each part checked before the next.

milestones.title: Phase 16 — Reels from your footage
milestones.goal: Turn a long, unedited video (an unboxing, a tutorial, a talk) into a finished 30-second reel with little or no hand work: the shots chosen, framed vertically, cut on the beat and captioned. Today each of those steps is done by hand.

tasks.title: Make a reel from this video
tasks.detail: An AI Dev Kit add-on watches a long video and finds the moments worth keeping (products shown clearly, reveals, steady and sharp shots, what is being talked about), then builds a cut of the length asked for on the music's beats, with a title for each part. Every chosen shot stays an ordinary clip that can be swapped, trimmed or moved.

tasks.title: Landscape to vertical, following the subject
tasks.detail: Reframe 16:9 footage to 9:16 (or 1:1, 4:5) with the crop following a face, hands or the product, smoothly, building on the face tracking the Studio already has. The crop path is editable afterwards.

tasks.title: Caption style packs
tasks.detail: Seven caption styles in one click (Bold, Neon, Chrome, Handwritten, Karaoke, Boxed, Giant), each with its font added for you; a new Letters setting on captions (outline, soft shadow, neon glow, chrome); and Use this style on every caption.

tasks.title: Edit by the words
tasks.detail: Strike words out of a transcript (or let Mark ums and repeats do it, with long pauses shortened) and the voice-over, its footage and the cut-out person are cut together, with what comes after moved earlier; captions follow every part.

tasks.title: One-click effect stacks
tasks.detail: Five stacks in one click (Punch-in, Beat drop, Glitch hit, Impact, Whip in), each a set of ordinary clips with its sound, added at the playhead and moved onto the nearest beat of the music.

tasks.title: Title behind the subject
tasks.detail: One click on a text layer (Behind the person) puts it between the footage and the person cut out of it, cutting the person out first when needed, so the person stands in front of the title.

tasks.title: One scene, many videos from data
tasks.detail: Bind a scene's words, pictures and numbers to a spreadsheet (products, prices, photos) and render one video per row: a reel for every product in a shop, from one design.

tasks.title: Free stock footage search
tasks.detail: Search free stock libraries and open archives for real video clips (and pictures) from inside the Studio, with their licences shown, and drop them on the timeline; for people with no footage of their own.

tasks.title: Choose the cut-out method
tasks.detail: A setting for how people are cut out of footage, to try what suits each video: Standard (fine edges on the graphics card, the default), Fast (a quick body outline, for drafts) and Robust Video Matting (very fast and steady, an optional download because of its licence). Each says what it is good at and whether it is installed. Person and what they hold (SAM 2) is its own item below.

tasks.title: Cut out the person and what they hold
tasks.detail: A fourth cut-out method (SAM 2): click the person and the product once, and both are followed and cut out through the whole video, for product demos where the thing in the hand matters as much as the face.

milestones.title: Phase 17 — Direct by pointing
milestones.goal: Make changing a scene with AI as precise as pointing: say what to change where it is, choose a direction before anything is built, and let measurements, not impressions, decide whether a frame is right.

tasks.title: Point at the frame to change it
tasks.detail: Click a spot in the preview and write what to change. AI assist receives the moment, the element under the pointer and a close-up of that area, changes only that, and answers in a sentence; the preview stays where it was. The values it touches (a title, a number, a colour, a hold time) appear as fields to adjust by hand.

tasks.title: Three directions first
tasks.detail: For a new scene, AI assist first proposes three short directions (mood, pace, look, with a still for each) and builds the one chosen, instead of committing to the first idea.

tasks.title: Music composed to the scene
tasks.detail: Alongside ACE-Step, a local composer that writes a short score to the scene's own timing (accents where things land, a lift at the reveal) and plays it with sampled instruments, on any computer, no graphics card needed.

tasks.title: Measurements overrule impressions
tasks.detail: When the AI reviews its frames (Look and fix), the measured layout check has the last word: text that overflows, captions outside the safe area or overlapping parts are fixed even if the frame looks fine to the AI. The layout check also measures captions.

tasks.title: Motion blur in videos
tasks.detail: An option when rendering a video to blend sub-frames, so fast moves look filmed rather than stepped.

tasks.title: Finish in another editor
tasks.detail: Export a scene's cut, sound and captions as a project other editors open (for example CapCut, Premiere or DaVinci Resolve), as well as the finished video.

tasks.title: Make one like this
tasks.detail: Give the AI a video you like: it works out its structure, pacing, text style, cuts and use of music, and builds your scene to the same shape with your own content.

tasks.title: Better motion rules, and smoother colour
tasks.detail: Fold proven motion-design principles (timing and easing, shot composition, cutting to the beat, restraint) into the rules AI assist follows, and blend colours through OKLCH so colour changes and gradients stay bright instead of passing through grey.

milestones.title: Phase 18 — More to animate
milestones.goal: More kinds of material to bring into a scene: vector animations from the large free libraries, and 3D objects made from a description.

tasks.title: Lottie animations
tasks.detail: A Lottie layer: drop in an animation from the free libraries, play it on the scene's clock, and recolour or reword it in place.

tasks.title: 3D objects from a description
tasks.detail: Describe an object and the AI Dev Kit builds it as a 3D model for a 3D layer, checking each attempt by measurement (sizes, parts that touch, nothing intersecting) and by looking at it from several sides, and keeping the best. Replaces the planned Blender add-on as the first route; Blender stays as an option.

tasks.title: See the camera's path
tasks.detail: In 3D layers, show the camera's route and field of view in the scene, so a camera move can be shaped by eye.

milestones.title: Phase 19 — Motion styles, and a stricter review
milestones.goal: Let people ask for a recognised motion-design style by name ("make it synthwave", "line-art style") and get the real thing, and have AI assist judge its own work as hard as a design jury would. Built from published motion-design style collections (an MIT-licensed set of fifteen styles with a working method and a review rubric, credited in the guide, and public catalogues of further styles), written in our own words for what the Studio can build.

tasks.title: A motion-styles guide for AI assist
tasks.detail: About two dozen styles written down the way AI assist can use them: what makes each recognisable at a glance and how to build it from the Studio's presets, layers, fonts and colours. Ready now: flat vector, line art, isometric, 3D, toy and material 3D, Bauhaus, Swiss grid and kinetic type, synthwave, aurora glass, collage, HUD and terminal, dark tech keynote, data story, living UI screencast and vertical social captions. In the AI Dev Kit and the Studio's AI skill, and choosable as a style in AI assist's settings.

tasks.title: A film's shape: hook, hero moment, end frame
tasks.detail: AI assist plans every scene the same way: something happening in the first half-second, one unmistakable hero moment around two-thirds of the way through, and a composed end frame held about a second with gentle movement; still key frames checked before the motion is built, and sound hits on the same cue times as the picture.

tasks.title: Look and fix, judged like a jury
tasks.detail: The review scores the frames on seven points (style fidelity, the idea and its wow, motion craft, design and typography, finish, sound and sync, technical), then fixes the weakest first, each fix tied to a moment with concrete numbers. Measured problems still overrule impressions. It looks at enough frames to judge motion, not one still.

tasks.title: The effects some styles need
tasks.detail: New player effects for the styles that cannot be built yet: a frame-by-frame line "boil" (hand-drawn cel animation), shapes morphing into one another (liquid and morph), pixelation (pixel art), brush strokes painting on over paper texture (watercolour and ink), halftone dots and offset colour plates (risograph print), and scanlines with colour bleed (VHS and CRT, beyond today's film look). Alongside the planned text looks: outline, 3D offset shadow, gradient letters and skew.

tasks.title: Styles as starting points
tasks.detail: Each style also as a short ready-made scene in the library, made with the Studio and passing its own review, to open and make your own.

tasks.title: Benchmarked against real films
tasks.detail: Give AI assist the same kinds of brief that people publish films for (an app launch, a logo reveal, a poster breaking out of its frame, a history in thirty seconds, a wordless explainer) and compare the results side by side; the gaps become fixes. The published films are only used as a reference, never copied.

milestones.title: Phase 20 — Real screen demos, made in minutes
milestones.goal: Tutorials and promos that show the real product working, recorded and framed automatically: a short step list in, a sharp, zoomed, captioned reel out. Real screen footage reads as genuine in a way generated graphics alone do not.

tasks.title: Screencast recorder
tasks.detail: The AI Dev Kit runs a list of steps in a real browser the way a person would (a visible cursor with click ripples, natural mouse moves, typing, real drags) and records it sharp (2x), carried across page loads with the waiting cut out, plus when and where each step happened.

tasks.title: Unyson+ actions
tasks.detail: Ready-made steps that know the WordPress admin and the page builder: name the page, add a section, drag in an element, open its settings, fill a field, save, preview. A demo is a few lines.

tasks.title: Automatic zoom
tasks.detail: The recording becomes a scene whose camera zooms to each action where it happens and pulls back between them, with numbered step captions, an optional title, end card and music, in 9:16 or 16:9.

tasks.title: A styled demo site
tasks.detail: A copy of a designed site kept for demos, with a snapshot of its database and uploads and a one-command reset, so every recording starts from the same clean site and ends on a page worth showing. How to set one up is in the screencasts guide.

tasks.title: Screenshots with highlights
tasks.detail: Sharp 2x shots of any page or element, with an optional highlight, arrow, blur or callout, for explainers, thumbnails and the docs.

tasks.title: Screencasts in the Studio
tasks.detail: Drop a recording into Kinetic Scenes and it arrives framed: browser frame, the automatic zooms as camera keys you can adjust, the cursor and the step captions.

milestones.title: Phase 21 — Projects you share with your AI agent
milestones.goal: Kinetic Scenes and an AI agent work on the same video: projects are folders on your computer, the Studio shows what the agent makes as it makes it, and you preview and export it yourself.

tasks.title: Projects as folders
tasks.detail: A workspace kept by the AI Dev Kit (Documents/Kinetic Scenes, or a folder you choose): each project is scene.json, media/ and renders/. File › Projects opens one or makes one from the scene in front of you.

tasks.title: Saved as you work, changes followed live
tasks.detail: The Studio saves into the folder as you work and writes footage, music and voice into media/. When an agent changes the project, the open Studio updates at once (one Undo goes back).

tasks.title: Agent tools for projects
tasks.detail: project_list and project_save on the Kinetic Scenes MCP tools, and studio-cli project: an agent puts a scene and every file it uses into a project and gives you a link that opens it.

tasks.title: Connect your AI agent
tasks.detail: The Studio says where the fuller result comes from: an agent connected through the AI Dev Kit records, narrates, makes music and checks frames; AI assist stays for quick ideas and small changes.

tasks.title: AI assist that works in steps
tasks.detail: With a project open and Claude Code in the AI Dev Kit, AI assist runs as an agent in the project folder with the Kinetic Scenes tools: it reads the notes, edits the scene, looks at frames, checks its work and adds to the notes, and each step shows in the chat as it happens. It cannot run commands, reach the web or render.

milestones.title: Phase 22 — Agents that edit like a careful person
milestones.goal: An AI agent working in a Kinetic Scenes project remembers where it left off, sees timing at a glance, checks every cut before showing you, cleans up spoken footage, and installs in one step.

tasks.title: Faster renders on your graphics card
tasks.detail: Video export through the AI Dev Kit draws frames on the strongest graphics card the computer has, encodes with its hardware encoder (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or Apple) when that works, takes frames in several browsers at once, and first makes footage easy to seek. 10 seconds with a screen recording: 35 s of frames became 6.5 s.

tasks.title: Project notes
tasks.detail: Each project keeps a notes.md beside scene.json: the plan, what was approved, what is left. A later session, or another agent, carries on from it.

tasks.title: A timeline at a glance
tasks.detail: One picture of a stretch of the video: a strip of frames, the sound wave and every spoken word at its time, so an agent places cuts, captions and narration where they belong without pulling dozens of frames.

tasks.title: Every cut checked
tasks.detail: After a render the kit checks the finished video: every voice line heard at its time, no unintended black, loudness about -14 LUFS and no clipping, and reports what to fix before it is shown. Clicks are prevented where they start: every sound clip fades in and out by at least 12 ms.

tasks.title: Clean up spoken footage
tasks.detail: From the words and their times: false starts, um / uh and long pauses cut, each cut faded, with an edit list; and the best of several takes of a line chosen by the voice check. Speech recognition runs on your own computer.

tasks.title: Connect your agents in one step
tasks.detail: The first time the AI Dev Kit starts, it asks whether to connect the AI agents it finds (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex): yes registers the Kinetic Scenes tools with each and adds the skill to Claude Code. Or run studio-cli connect.

milestones.title: Phase 23 — Learn from great reels
milestones.goal: Make outreach and client reels faster and better paced by learning from finished reels: read the rhythm of a reel we admire, describe a reel in a few beats, and show how a reel was built. The ideas come from studying an open-source motion-breakdown tool; the code is our own.

tasks.title: Learn the rhythm of a reference reel
tasks.detail: Import a reference video, find its cuts with FFmpeg scene detection, and save a timing map and a contact sheet. A new scene can then follow the same cut points and section lengths, so it is paced like a reel that already works. Shipped as the `reference` command and the `video_reference` agent tool: hard cuts plus motion peaks (reveals and transitions), the pace in words, sections, a numbered contact sheet, and rhythm markers on a scene. See [Learn the rhythm of a reel](/kinetic-scenes/reference-rhythm).

tasks.title: Beats: describe a reel in a few lines
tasks.detail: A small set of beat kinds (headline, logo reveal, photo in a mask, split frame, list, rating or proof, closing frame with the credit) that build a full scene in the client's brand. A brief becomes about eight lines of beats instead of a hand-built scene. Shipped as the `beats` command and the `scene_from_beats` agent tool: seven beat kinds, layouts clear of the apps' buttons, the credit on the closing frame, and beat starts snapped to a reference rhythm. See [Beats](/kinetic-scenes/beats).

tasks.title: Breakdown view
tasks.detail: Play a finished reel on top and its storyboard beats underneath, in sync, and export it as a "how this reel was made" video for pitches and Kinetic Scenes marketing.

tasks.title: Test a frame-accurate export in the browser
tasks.detail: A trial of exporting in the browser with WebCodecs, encoding every frame at its own timestamp, compared with the current render time. It ships only if it is faster without losing quality. Result (2026-10-28): the Studio's existing in-browser export (it seeks each frame exactly and encodes with WebCodecs) rendered the 38 s demo in 31 s against the kit's 46 s, at matching quality once a 3D placement bug was fixed (Studio 0.0.97). The kit stays the default because the browser path needs Chrome's HTML-in-Canvas, which is still behind a flag.

tasks.title: A friendlier public repository
tasks.detail: An animated demo at the top of the README, a one-command start, a FAQ, issue forms and labelled starter issues, so new users and contributors can get going quickly.
